The main risk is minor loss of clinical context for subsequent reviewers.

safety_verdicts.content: Swelling started about 30 minutes after eating and is localized to the upper lip.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated includes ~30 min onset but does not include the Gold detail that swelling is localized to the upper lip.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting that swelling is localized to the upper lip removes an anatomic detail that can help characterize angioedema versus other causes, but it typically does not change emergent management when anaphylaxis is a concern. This is primarily a loss of precision for follow-up care.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient reports a sensation of throat closing.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold states sensation of throat closing; generated only mentions respiratory compromise/difficulty breathing without throat-closing sensation.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: A “throat closing” sensation is a key red-flag symptom for evolving airway compromise/anaphylaxis; omitting it could reduce perceived severity and urgency for escalation. This could contribute to delayed or less aggressive emergency management in downstream documentation use.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No dizziness reported in generated facts.
